# Platform Foundation Requirements Review Checklist

**Purpose**: Formal pre-Tasks review of the quality, completeness, consistency, and boundedness of the approved Platform Foundation requirements and planning decisions
**Created**: 2026-10-06
**Feature**: [Platform Foundation specification](../spec.md)
**Gate**: After Plan and before Tasks
**Audience**: Product Owner / independent technical reviewer

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Authority, Scope, and Boundedness

- [x] CHK001 Are the minimum foundation outcomes distinguished clearly enough from later Product capabilities that Feature 001 cannot be read as authorizing Homepage composition, Search, editorial content, migration, analytics, or any named content model? [Completeness, Spec §Scope Boundaries; Plan §Deferred Work]
- [x] CHK002 Do the in-scope and explicitly out-of-scope statements collectively preserve every Product Owner exclusion without introducing an implicit route around those exclusions elsewhere in the planning artifacts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019 and §Scope Boundaries; Plan §Summary and §Deferred Work]
- [x] CHK003 Is “minimum public verification behavior” defined narrowly and consistently as a foundation surface rather than a preliminary Homepage or public-site feature? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 1 and §Assumptions; Plan §One Astro + EmDash platform; Research §1]
- [x] CHK004 Is the governed evolution rule clear that later approved work may change a boundary only after a demonstrated gap and amendment of the owning authority, while still prohibiting a second competing foundation? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 4, FR-017, and SC-007]
- [x] CHK005 [Gap] Is the specification's `Status: Draft` reconciled with its treatment as the approved input to this pre-Tasks gate, including who records Product Owner approval and where that approval is authoritative? [Spec header; Constitution §V]

## Platform-Native Design and Extension Limits

- [x] CHK006 Does every planned foundation capability identify the native Astro, EmDash, PostgreSQL, or Quadlet path that satisfies it before any Songhealth-specific extension is considered? [Traceability, Plan §Architecture and Implementation Approach; Research §§1, 3–8]
- [x] CHK007 Is the sole demonstrated custom gap stated precisely as the absence of one aggregate foundation ready/not-ready signal, with evidence that native capabilities do not already provide it? [Justification, Spec §FR-016; Plan §Runtime verification and readiness; Research §7]
- [x] CHK008 Are the permitted responsibilities of the readiness helper bounded tightly enough that later tasks cannot expand it into a health API, monitoring or observability framework, service layer, plugin framework, or public endpoint? [Boundedness, Plan §Runtime verification and readiness; Research §7]
- [x] CHK009 Is the explicit empty EmDash seed described consistently as scope control—not a Product schema—and are default Posts/Pages and all Songhealth collections clearly excluded? [Clarity, Plan §One Astro + EmDash platform; Research §3; Data Model §2]
- [x] CHK010 Does the planned structure foreclose authorization for a separate backend/API server, Domain/Application/Policy layers, repository/service wrappers, custom RBAC, custom media/search/redirect/import subsystems, Redis, brokers, microservices, Kubernetes, or a generic platform framework? [Over-engineering, Spec §FR-019 and §Explicitly Out of Scope; Plan §Project Structure; Constitution §II]

## Runtime, Persistence, Configuration, and Readiness

- [x] CHK011 Are the responsibilities and boundaries of the single Astro + EmDash runtime, PostgreSQL state, and persistent media bytes defined without overlap or an unowned persistence concern? [Completeness, Plan §Summary and §Production topology and durability; Data Model §§2 and 4]
- [x] CHK012 Is “runtime recreation” defined consistently as replacing ephemeral runtime components while retaining explicitly attached database and media persistence, with missing attachments unable to masquerade as a healthy empty system? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases and §Assumptions; Plan §Production topology and durability]
- [x] CHK013 Is the production database boundary unambiguous that PostgreSQL has no public host exposure and is reachable only through the approved private application/deployment path? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010 and SC-003; Plan §Production topology and durability; current/10 §3.1]
- [x] CHK014 Are environment-specific configuration, secret classification, redaction, external injection, and prohibition from Git/images/artifacts described consistently across all artifacts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007 and FR-012; Plan §Configuration and secrets; Data Model §1]
- [x] CHK015 Is public-runtime availability kept conceptually and observably separate from operational ready/not-ready state, with no wording that implies a publicly exposed readiness endpoint? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications, FR-003, and FR-011; Plan §Runtime verification and readiness; Research §7]
- [x] CHK016 [Ambiguity] Are the required readiness dependencies and timing semantics clear across recurring probes, release/start migration checks, and one-time media writeability checks, including which failure prevents readiness and which evidence is evaluated separately? [Spec §FR-011 and SC-004; Plan §Runtime verification and readiness; Data Model §5; Quickstart §3]

## Recovery, Secrets, and Data Protection

- [x] CHK017 Is the logical PostgreSQL recovery scope stated as a complete, unfiltered EmDash database archive restored into a clean database, without implying cluster-global role recovery or a partial content export? [Completeness, Plan §Backup, restore, and secret recovery; Research §9; Data Model §6]
- [x] CHK018 [Conflict] Is the Product Owner's bounded Feature 001 decision for logical recovery visibly identified as higher-authority than the broader physical-backup/PITR baseline in `current/10`, without silently changing that blueprint for future operational features? [Authority, Plan §Constitution Check and §Deferred Work; Research §9; current/10 §18]
- [x] CHK019 Is the association of database and media artifacts with one known validation state sufficiently specified while explicitly avoiding any promise of atomic or transactionally synchronized cross-store backup? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications, FR-013, and §Recovery Set; Plan §Backup, restore, and secret recovery; Data Model §6]
- [x] CHK020 Is independently protected runtime-secret recovery clearly required for recovery readiness while remaining outside the database/media Recovery Set and outside Git, planning artifacts, transcripts, and review evidence? [Consistency, Plan §Configuration and secrets and §Backup, restore, and secret recovery; Research §10; Data Model §7]
- [x] CHK021 Does the recovery boundary explicitly exclude PITR, WAL archiving, replication privileges, standby servers, continuous backup orchestration, atomic snapshots, and new RTO/RPO commitments unless later authority adds them? [Scope, Plan §Technical Context and §Deferred Work; Research §9; Quickstart §7]
- [x] CHK022 Are database-record and media-integrity outcomes objectively measurable as 100% recovery with zero unexplained differences, without adding arbitrary time targets, ratings, retention promises, or other unapproved SLAs? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005; Plan §Verification and Independent Review; Data Model §6]
- [x] CHK023 Are all validation records, media, identities, and recovery evidence restricted to disposable non-confidential/public-publishable data, with native EmDash authentication and least privilege used without custom RBAC? [Security, Spec §FR-018 and §Assumptions; Plan §Configuration and secrets; Research §6; current/10 §§6, 11, and 19]

## Development, Production, and Version Assumptions

- [x] CHK024 Is the development path explicitly simpler than production—native Node/npm/Astro/agent tooling with Podman only where useful for database parity—without becoming a second deployment architecture? [Clarity, Plan §Development path; current/10 §§3.1 and 20]
- [x] CHK025 Is rootless Podman plus systemd Quadlet consistently the sole production container/lifecycle baseline, with Docker/Compose and Kubernetes excluded rather than maintained in parallel? [Consistency, Plan §Technical Context and §Production topology and durability; current/10 §§2, 3.1, and 23]
- [x] CHK026 Are reverse-proxy product selection, monitoring-stack selection, hosting-provider choice, and unrelated infrastructure explicitly deferred while their required security and operational boundaries remain stated? [Scope, Spec §Explicitly Out of Scope and §Assumptions; Plan §Production topology and durability and §Deferred Work; current/00 §1.1]
- [x] CHK027 Are version-sensitive Node, Astro, EmDash, PostgreSQL, package-manager, Podman, and Quadlet assumptions supported by dated authoritative research, separated from Product requirements, and subject to implementation-time revalidation and exact pinning? [Traceability, Plan §Technical Context; Research §§1, 2, 4, and 8]
- [x] CHK028 [Assumption] Is the unresolved EmDash/PostgreSQL 18 major-version compatibility risk framed as a fail-fast gate with a defined authority/escalation path, rather than permission to invent a workaround or silently change the approved baseline? [Research §4; Plan §Technical Context and §Constitution Check]

## Acceptance Quality and Cross-Artifact Consistency

- [x] CHK029 Do the success criteria collectively cover reproducible clean-checkout setup, public/Admin availability, readiness semantics, persistence/lifecycle durability, private database access, recovery integrity, and governed downstream extensibility without arbitrary Product SLAs? [Completeness and measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-008]
- [x] CHK030 Can an independent reviewer determine acceptance solely from the named evidence and criteria, while all supporting artifacts remain subordinate to current authority, assumptions stay distinct from requirements, foundation data concepts stay non-Product, and no external contract is invented? [Measurability and cross-artifact consistency, Spec §FR-015, SC-006, and §Assumptions; Plan §Constitution Check, §Project Structure, and §Verification and Independent Review; Data Model §Boundary Summary; Research §12; Quickstart §§Prerequisites and 8]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline and link to the relevant authority or planning artifact.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
